posts: Weekly check (2026-10-12): news sites and the third-party tracking services they contact before you click anything. 41 of 48 sites measured, from GitHub servers in the US. Most: The Independent 97, Daily Mirror 94, Evening Standard 93. Thread below.

By country, the median number of tracking services contacted before any click, with the sites measured in brackets: DE 1 (11), ES 10 (10), UK 76 (10), US 48 (8). All measured from GitHub servers in the US: sites that show their consent banner only to European visitors look worse here.
Spanish outlets, measured from a PC in Spain (2026-10-08): 12 of 12 sites measured. Most tracking services contacted before any click: El Mundo 22, Marca 12, elDiario.es 11.

Changes since last week (stable in most passes): New York Post +a-mo.net, agkn.com -ads.linkedin.com, bttrack.com; BBC News +2mdn.net, 360yield.com; CBS Sports -appier.net, onetag-sys.com; elDiario.es +doubleclick.net; ESPN +quantserve.com, sitescout.com -creativecdn.com, criteo.com (+11 more).

How: pages load with no clicks for 12s, 3 passes, median. Third party = other registered domain, matched to a limited list (may be incomplete). 7 sites blocked/unmeasured; 2 low-confidence not ranked. Counts, not legal verdicts. Method and data: https://joseasenjo.github.io/tracker-watch/
alt_text: Bar chart of the number of third-party tracking services contacted before any interaction, measurement of 2026-10-12. The Independent: 97; Daily Mirror: 94; Evening Standard: 93; The Times: 90; USA Today: 89; New York Post: 82.
